stem: Bilal has iron filings mixed with rice flour and wants a quick clean-up without picking each bit by hand. He also has aluminium foil scraps mixed with sand.

parts.text: Which claim correctly decides when magnetic separation is suitable?

options.text: A magnet can separate the iron filings from the rice flour.
A magnet can separate the aluminium foil scraps from the sand.
Magnetic separation cannot remove the iron filings because they are too small to pick up individually.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Iron is magnetic, so a magnet pulls iron filings out of rice flour; aluminium is not magnetic, so a magnet will not separate foil from sand, and small size alone does not block magnetic separation.

teacher.key_rationale: Magnetic separation works when one substance is magnetic (iron filings) and the other is not. Aluminium is not magnetic. Tiny iron pieces can still be lifted by a magnet.
